sn47.13:1.1: This event follows [sn47.12]() at Nāḷandā and precedes [sn47.14]() at Ukkacelā on the Vajjian shore of the Ganges, so the Buddha must have been somewhere on the road between them, not in Sāvatthī. Sāvatthī was the default location for teachings and it is often ascribed as a matter of convention.
sn47.13:1.3: The commentaries identify “novice Cunda”, who reported the deaths of Sāriputta ([sn47.13:1.3]()) and Mahāvīra ([dn29:2.1](), [mn104:3.1]()), as Sāriputta’s younger brother, explaining that the title “novice” was a nickname that persisted from the time he ordained as a young novice. The commentaries further identify him with Mahācunda, one of the great disciples ([mn118:](), [an6.17](), [mn8]()), who later brought the Dhamma to the land of the Cetīs ([an6.46](), [an10.24]()), and once stayed with Channa and Sāriputta ([mn144:4.1](), [sn35.87:1.2]()).
sn47.13:2.2: Sāriputta’s passing is treated with simplicity and dignity. There is no mention of relics, or any supernatural occurrences.
sn47.13:5.6: Text’s _otiṇṇo_ appears to be an error and I ignore it.
